League league phase, and discussed his reunion with his former club and his desire to continue helping the Eagles. 04 November 2026, 18h22 Copy link Kamiński Football Continue reading PREVIEW In the preview of the  Benfica -Lech Poznan, match—a clash in Matchday 4 of the league phase of the  Europa League , scheduled for 8:00 p.m. on Thursday, November 5, at Estádio da Luz—Kamiński anticipated a challenging match and expressed his ambition to help the Eagles secure another European victory. How does it feel to face a team you know so well? It’s very special, because it’s the club that gave me everything. I spent four years in the youth system and three years on the first team, where I won a championship. Then I took the next step in my career, moving to the Bundesliga. It’s very, very special for me to play against some of my former teammates. I know everyone at the club, so it will be a very special game for me. Do you have friends at the club? Have you talked to them? What did you talk about with the players and your friends at the club? Yes, of course. The president and all the players I’ve played with. Not all of them, because the team changes every year, but I’ve played with some of them. They’re my teammates, and of course they’re also very happy to come here and play against a great team like Benfica. How do you feel right now on the team and about the coach’s ideas? Compared to the first few months and the start of the season, do you think you’re in a better situation now? Yes, of course. I’m starting to feel like I’m improving. At the start of the season, maybe I wasn’t in the best shape. I felt like I wasn’t physically at my best yet. But with every training session, I’ve been getting better. Unfortunately, I got injured last month, and this past month has been a bit difficult getting back into shape. I work hard every day to improve and be ready so the coach will give me a chance on the field, as he did in Milan. I’ve been training a lot, and I’m definitely waiting for my chance.   You've said before that you don't give up in the face of competition within the team. Right now, do you feel ready to fight for a spot again? Do you have the mental strength for that? I think everyone knows what I’m like and knows that I never give up. That’s always been my motto, no matter what happens. I’m here for the coach, the Club, and the team, because, for me, Benfica is what matters most. Naturally, we want to achieve something special this season, and we need everyone. It’s normal for some players to get more playing time than others, but everyone wants to give the coach a reason to pick them and give them a chance. I’m someone who never gives up, and I’ll definitely keep fighting. I’m ready to come back from my injury. I’ve been working hard and training every day to earn another chance. From a more tactical perspective, what kind of team will you face? You know Lech Poznan very well. What challenges might they pose for Benfica? I’ve been following Lech in the Ekstraklasa and also in the Europa League. They’re different kinds of games because, in the league, they usually dominate their opponents, play in the opponent’s midfield, and look to control possession. But they’re a team that isn’t afraid to play and will also want to show their quality against us. So, it’ll be a really good game. I think it’ll be very open. I’m looking forward to playing. You played in the last match between Benfica and Lech Poznan six years ago, but on the Polish team’s side. From a tactical standpoint, how would you assess your development as a player since then? Back then, I was very young and had the opportunity to face a team as great as Benfica. It was a fantastic experience for me. Unfortunately, there were no fans in the stands due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and we played behind closed doors. But it was very special to face such talented players representing Benfica. Today, I’m a different and more experienced player. I’ve played for the national team, competed in the World Cup, and had other experiences. I’ve grown both as a player and as a man. So, while that moment was very special, I’m naturally a different player today. "They're a team that isn't afraid to play and that will also want to show what they're capable of against us" Given your knowledge of the opponent, you’ve already identified some of their strengths, but how should Benfica play? How can you help? Will you play tomorrow [Thursday]? If we play as we usually do, we’re the favorites in this match. That’s for sure. We’ll look to dominate Lech and push them back into a deeper defensive block. When we play at Estádio da Luz, we usually dominate our opponents. If they try to push forward, we can’t let them. We want to maintain possession in the opponent’s midfield and be patient to create good scoring opportunities. I think the game will play out that way, but we obviously have to be on guard against Lech’s counterattacks. What has it been like for you to compete for a spot on the team alongside players like Prestianni, Schjelderup, Lukebakio, and Rafa? And how has that contributed to your development? For me, it’s very important to compete for a spot on the team alongside players as good as the ones we have. It’s very positive for everyone. Plus, all the wingers have different strengths, which is also good for the team. In every game, the coach can choose the player he thinks is ready and who could be a good fit for that match. For me, it’s great to compete every week—and in every training session—with players of such high caliber. It’s an experience I’ll carry with me, and it will undoubtedly be an asset for my future. Following the big Serie A clash, the Rossoneri face another important and challenging test in the Europa League . AC Milan will look to bounce back on League Phase Matchday 4, scheduled for Thursday, November 5th at 6:45 PM CET at San Siro. At Milanello , following the final training session, Head Coach Rúben Amorim and Koni De Winter held their pre-match press conference. AMORIM FROM THE DERBY TO THE EUROPA LEAGUE "The Derby is in the past, now we have to focus on the Europa League. It was great to win, even though I'm still frustrated about the loss to Bologna. Tomorrow we need to be stronger to win. It doesn't matter who you are playing against, we want to get a result and go all the way in the competition." POSSIBLE OPTIONS "This is an important game, but we also need to be careful with certain players. We can't afford to lose any. Sometimes if you don't let players rest they can pick up injuries. So we need to rotate the squad, while recognizing that we need to win this game against a strong side who already have 9 points in this competition." PERFORMANCE "In the Europa League, for various reasons, we haven't been able to find consistency. Every game is different. We have three points in the competition and tomorrow we absolutely have to win. We've faced some difficulties, and I'm not entirely satisfied with our performances in the Europa League or in Serie A, where we should have more points." THE OPPONENTS "First of all, they are a team that is used to winning, regardless of the circumstances, and that gives them confidence. They are doing very well in the league. They play a 4-2-3-1 formation, have a strong identity, know how to play and are very comfortable in their style. They are coming to San Siro with nothing to lose, so the responsibility is on us. I've already told the players that we need to show the same approach that we had in the Derby. We are capable of winning or losing any game, it all depends on us." DEFENSIVE APPROACH "We defended well against Inter which allowed us to make better decisions. We need to do the same tomorrow. Diawara is working very well. He's had a long spell out of the team, but he's quick, strong and has great potential to improve." DE WINTER RECENT EMOTIONS "Becoming a father is an incredible feeling. I feel increasingly important on the pitch and I can sense that more trust is being placed in me. I think this is a great period in my career." ALWAYS READY TO PLAY "I feel good both physically and mentally. When there are lots of games, it's great to work hard so that I'm always ready to play. I enjoy it and always try to be prepared for every match." THE UNDERSTANDING WITH PAVLO "I feel comfortable playing alongside any of my teammates in defense. We've trained a lot and now we all know each other very well. It's great to play with Pavlo. He's a very good player and we always understand each other." THE OPPONENTS "They're doing very well and are full of confidence. We'll give everything to keep a clean sheet and beat them. We know it won't be easy." ROLE MODEL "If I had to name one player, I'd say Thiago Silva. He played for AC Milan, I've followed him closely and he's a fantastic player." The Bianconeri beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium in their Serie A Matchday 10 encounter. THE MATCH REPORT The game got off to a high-tempo start. In the seventh minute, Vicario showed excellent reflexes to deny Lucca's effort on the turn and keep the visitors at bay. As the minutes passed, Juventus began to find their rhythm going forward and, in the 27th minute, Juan Cabal rose highest to meet a Douglas Luiz corner, only to see his powerful header strike the post. Three minutes later, Spalletti's side came close to breaking the deadlock again following a fine team move: Kolo Muani burst past his marker down the flank and delivered an inviting cross for Alajbegovic, who connected with a first-time volley but sent his effort over the crossbar. Just before the break, Alajbegovic had another opportunity to put the Bianconeri ahead, but Meret managed to parry his left-footed strike away. The first half ended goalless at the Allianz Stadium. After a closely contested start to the second half, the breakthrough finally came in the 70th minute. Zhegrova produced a moment of brilliance, beating Rrahmani with a superb piece of skill before finding Alajbegovic. The young talent took matters into his own hands, cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot beyond Meret's reach to send the Allianz Stadium into raptures and give Juventus the lead. Things went from bad to worse for Napoli five minutes later when Marianucci, already on a yellow card, fouled Cabal and was shown a second yellow, followed by a red card. Juventus continued to push forward and doubled their advantage in the 87th minute. A flowing team move saw the ball worked out to Boga on the left, who cut inside onto his right foot and curled his effort into the far corner, leaving Meret beaten. Alajbegovic and Boga sealed the victory as Juventus marked their 129th birthday with three points. text: Ahead of Marseille match: Martínez sees upturn at OM – Medina on key factors against former club | Bayer04.de Back 4.11.2026 - Europa League Share Ahead of Marseille match: Martínez sees upturn at OM – Medina on key factors against former club The Europa League campaign continues: Bayer 04 host Olympique Marseille at the BayArena on matchday four of the group stage on Thursday 5 November (kick-off: 21:00 CET). Ahead of the clash against the club from the French Mediterranean coast, head coach Carles Martínez spoke about the visitors’ form and had some good news regarding the squad. Former OM player Facundo Medina spoke, amongst other things, about the factors that will be crucial against his old club. “Marseille are a top club; we have great respect for them,” said Carles Martínez at the pre-match press conference on Wednesday afternoon. The Spaniard added: “Yes, they still don’t have any points, but they are a very good side.” Marseille are currently 34th out of 36 in the UEL table, falling short of their own expectations. Martínez: “They made a lot of changes to their squad over the summer, and there was also a change of coaches. As I always say with regard to our own situation at Leverkusen: It’s about the process, and about improving a little bit every day. That, it seems to me, is what they’re managing to do.” One example of this is their recent run of four consecutive wins in Ligue 1, which has seen Marseille climb from second-bottom – having won just one of their previous five matches – to their current sixth-place position. And Martinez is well aware of this: “They’re a strong side; it will be a tough match.” Personnel: Flekken in goal – Badé in the squad Talking about the matchday squad, the coach revealed that Mark Flekken would be in goal and Loïc Badé will be back in the squad. Martínez went on to explain: “As for the other players currently unavailable, the situation varies. Regarding Kofi ( Christian Kofane , ed. ), we’re yet to make a decision. As for Eli ( Eliesse Ben Seghir , ed. ) and Guéla ( Guéla Doué , ed. ), we hope they will be back after the international break. But of course, you can’t say for certain.” Speaking about Kennet Eichhorn , who was back in training for the first time at Leverkusen this week , the Spaniard said: “He’ll be taking it step by step now. It’s difficult to say when the next steps will come. He’ll take them when he feels ready. The most important thing is that he’s in good spirits. And he is.” When asked about Facundo Medina , Martínez said: “When I spoke to him back then to persuade him to join us at Bayer 04, we talked a lot about his energy and attitude, which are a huge asset to any team. He brings so much to the team and is always pushing his teammates on. He’s not just here at Leverkusen to be a defensive player, but also to help out as a person through his attitude.” Display videos Yes, I'd like to see videos dispalyed. Activate now Medina: "think big, stay humble" The Argentine then took his place on the top table. The defender, who joined Leverkusen from Marseille in the summer, said of his former club: “They’re a team with lots of experienced players. It will be a physical battle and the small details will make all the difference. But if we go into the match with the right attitude, we will pick up the three points!” What matters most to the 27-year-old is: “We want to put right the mistakes we’ve made at times in recent matches.” When asked about the team’s objectives in the Europa League, Medina said: “I don’t like to talk about the future. We’re taking it one match at a time. Of course, we want to win every one of them and, ultimately, achieve the best possible result in every competition. We’re thinking big, but at the same time we’re staying humble.” On his fellow countryman Ezequiel Fernández , who has also been called up to the Argentina squad and who, after the weekend, will be away on international duty , Medina said: “I’m delighted to have been called up again, and even more so that Equi has been selected alongside me. text: Our next opponents: Marseille on the up, but still struggling in the Europa League | Bayer04.de Back 4.11.2026 - Europa League Share Our next opponents: Marseille on the up, but still struggling in the Europa League Olympique Marseille are really hitting their stride in Ligue 1. The nine-time French champions have fought their way back after a mixed start to the season and recently recorded four wins in a row. However, OM have no points in the Europa League so far this term. On Thursday, 5 November (kick-off: 21:00 CET), Marseille will be looking to change that at the BayArena. The lowdown on our next opponents. Position Olympique Marseille currently sit sixth in the Ligue 1 table on 15 points. Things looked very different after matchday 5, when OM were next to bottom. Then, following four consecutive defeats, a 2–0 win at Troyes marked a turning point. That was followed by victories against Angers and Le Havre. In their most recent 2–0 win at Toulouse, the attacking duo of Amine Harit and Amine Gouiri both scored in the first half. After the match, coach Bruno Genesio expressed his satisfaction with the result and his team’s performance. “We pressed well, particularly in the first half, and played consistently going forward. In the second half we sat back a little, but our commitment and attitude remained strong.” Despite the short winning streak in the league, the 60-year-old – who took over from Habib Beye in July this year – said the team must remain humble. Previously, Genesio managed FC Stade Rennes and, most recently, Lille. At Rennes, his players included Bayer 04 players Loic Badé and Martin Terrier.  Thanks to this resurgence, Marseille have closed the gap to just two points behind the Champions League places. In the Europa League, however, the club sit 34th in the group stage after three games, with zero points and a goal difference of 1 to 6. They started with a 4-1 defeat away to Besiktas, followed by two 1-0 losses against Olympiacos and Sturm Graz. The southern French side only secured their place in the competition on the final matchday of last season with a 3–1 win over their direct rivals, Stade Rennes.   Marseille have nil points in the Europa League so far – here’s a scene from their most recent 1-0 defeat at Sturm Graz. Personnel In front of goalkeeper Jeffrey de Lange, who came through the Ajax youth system, Genesio is relying on a wealth of experience in his back four. Captain Timothy Weah (26) is a regular at right-back. The American has made 53 international appearances and is a team-mate of Bayer 04’s Malik Tillman in the USA team. Weah has already won the French league title three times (twice with Paris Saint-Germain, once with Lille) and he lifted the Coppa Italia with Juventus. On the left flank, the experienced Emerson – EURO 2021 winner with Italy – is in defence. However, the 32-year-old had to be substituted on 17 minutes last Sunday due to knee problems. It is doubtful whether he will be fit to play at Leverkusen. In central defence this season, Morocco international Nayef Aguerd (30) and England U21 international CJ Egan-Riley have often been the first-choice pairing. Both featured several times last season alongside Werkself player Facundo Medina at the centre of the Marseille defence. The two midfielders Pierre-Emile Höjbjerg (31) and Amine Harit (29) are well known from the Bundesliga. Höjbjerg, captain of Denmark with 101 international caps to date, played for Bayern Munich, FC Augsburg and Schalke 04. Harit also played for the latter for several years. Alongside the pair, Angel Gomes and creative midfielder Himad Abdelli are among the regulars in midfield. Up front, Marseille have had to cope with the departure of their two top goalscorers from last season. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (10 goals) and Mason Greenwood (16) moved to Deportivo La Coruna and Fenerbahçe respectively in the summer. Centre-forward Amine Gouiri is currently OM’s top scorer. Ibrahim Maza’s Algeria team-mate has scored six goals in Ligue 1 so far and provided three assists.     Former Bundesliga players currently at Marseille: Pierre-Emile Höjbjerg and Amine Harit Problems Marseille repeatedly run into problems when the opposition press high. That was most recently the case in the Europa League in the 1-0 defeat at Sturm Graz. Under pressure, Marseille made a number of errors in their build-up play. One of these led to the decisive goal conceded early on. The team also struggled defensively in their 4–3 win against Le Havre in Ligue 1: OM were leading 4–0 but still had to hold their nerve to secure the victory in the end. In Ligue 1, Marseille have already conceded 13 goals in nine matches. In the Europa League, they have conceded six goals in three games to date.​​​ Performers Despite the departures of Aubameyang and Greenwood, the Marseille attack remains strong. After league leaders Paris Saint-Germain (21), Marseille (20) are currently joint second with Stade Rennes for the most goals scored in Ligue 1. Alongside Harit and Gouiri, the Brazilian Igor Paixao is also a strong dribbler and finisher in attack. Two years ago, the left-winger – then still playing for Feyenoord – faced the Werkself in the Champions League, a match which the Werkself won 4–0. Although Marseille currently sit third from bottom in the Europa League group stage, they are among the strongest-performing teams in the competition. In terms of possession, only Bayer 04 (58 per cent), Real Sociedad and AZ Alkmaar (both 57.3 per cent) have better figures than OM (56.7 per cent). Marseille are also among the top eight for completed passes, with 87.3 per cent. Now these impressive stats need to be backed up by results. “We’ll be travelling to Leverkusen to put in the best possible performance and get a result,” said Genesio ahead of the match at the BayArena.   Related News Bundesliga - 04.11.2026 Vote for Ibrahim Maza as Player of the Month for October 2026 Video game developer Electronic Arts (EA), in collaboration with the Bundesliga, has announced the six nominees for the Bundesliga Player of the Month award for October 2026 – and Bayer 04’s Ibrahim Maza is among them. Press Focus   Rywale pod lupą: SL Benfica Piłkarz, który z FC Barceloną wygrał na hiszpańskim podwórku każde trofeum, trener z bogatą przeszłością w Premier League czy jeden z najbardziej perspektywicznych argentyńskich skrzydłowych. Tradycyjnie przed meczem Ligi Europy z udziałem Lecha Poznań przedstawiamy wybrane postacie z ekipy najbliższego przeciwnika Kolejorza, a dziś na tapet wzięliśmy 38-krotnych mistrzów Portugalii, SL Benfikę. Marco Silva Przed trwającym sezonem 49-letni Portugalczykowi przyszło wejść w buty słynnego José Mourinho, który powrócił na ławkę Realu Madryt. Mający wielkie aspiracje klub ze stolicy zdecydował się sięgnąć po człowieka, który jadł chleb z niejednego trenerskiego pieca. Urodzony w Lizbonie szkoleniowiec zaczynał pracę w tej roli w Estoril, wypływając na szerokie wody i otrzymując w rezultacie angaż w jednym z krajowych gigantów, Sportingu CP. Z nim zdobył Puchar Portugalii, a kolejne trofeum do gabloty dołożył już w Grecji, zdobywając mistrzostwo z Olympiakosem w roku 2016. Swoją karierę kontynuował na Wyspach Brytyjskich w Hull City, Watfordzie, Evertonie oraz londyńskim Fulham. Ten ostatni zespół poprowadził w ponad 200 meczach, wywalczył z nim awans do Premier League w rozgrywkach 2021/22 oraz rywalizował z powodzeniem w jednej z najbardziej wymagających lig Starego Kontynentu przez cztery sezony. Od chwili objęcia Orłów Silva deklarował, że chce stworzyć zespół dominujący oraz nadający ton wydarzeniom boiskowym. Tamtejsze media podkreślają, że o ile ten proces jest w dalszym ciągu w toku, to już można w poczynaniach Benfiki stwierdzić poprawę jej postawy w ofensywie, co przekłada się na większą liczbę kreowanych szans i strzelonych goli. Fredrik Aursnes Jedną z pierwszych decyzji Silvy było powierzenie opaski kapitańskiej 30-letniemu Norwegowi, który zawodnikiem 38-krotnych mistrzów Portugalii pozostaje od czterech sezonów. Już jako nastolatek cieszył się w ojczyźnie z sensacyjnego zdobycia pucharu z IL Hødd, a jego ówczesna ekipa znajdowała się wtedy na zapleczu norweskiej ekstraklasy. Dalsza droga Aursnesa wiodła bardzo harmonijnie, bo po ponad pięciu latach w Molde przyszedł czas na transfer do Holandii, do Feyenoordu Rotterdam, a po kolejnej kampanii przeprowadzkę na Półwysep Iberyjski. Na nim budował konsekwentnie swoją pozycję, przyczynił się do tytułu w roku 2023 i pozostawał niezwykle istotnym punktem drugiej linii swojej drużyny. W niej może występować praktycznie w każdym miejscu, a kolejni trenerzy Benfiki cenią go za pracowitość, boiskową inteligencję oraz znaczenie dla budowania akcji. Co ciekawe, zaczynał jako młody chłopak od lekkoatletyki, a dobre przygotowanie motoryczne stanowi jedną z jego najmocniejszych cech. Vangelis Pavlidis Może być trudno w to uwierzyć, ale jego trafienie dające wygraną w poniedziałkowym starciu z Alvercą było już osiemnastym w trwającej kampanii. Grek błyszczy skutecznością, ale nie jest to niczym nowym, bo smykałkę do zdobywania bramek potwierdzał w zespole Orłów już w dwóch poprzednich sezonach, a także na wcześniejszych etapie kariery w AZ Alkmaar, w którym został królem strzelców Eredivisie w roku 2024. 27-letni napastnik to etatowy reprezentant Grecji, potrafi nie tylko wykorzystać dogranie z bocznych sektorów czy głębi pola, ale także samemu wykreować sobie oraz partnerom dogodną szansę. Lubi zejść po piłkę, uczestniczyć w rozegraniu, jednak pojawia się również w polu karnym rywali w idealnym momencie, by zaskoczyć ich defensywę. Cechuje go ruchliwość, zdolność do ciężkiej pracy w pressingu oraz przede wszystkim bardzo szeroki wachlarz finalizacji. Gianluca Prestianni Filigranowy skrzydłowy w obecnej kampanii stanowi jedną z najgroźniejszych broni w ofensywnych szeregach naszego czwartkowego przeciwnika. Sprowadzony przed blisko trzema laty z Velez Sarsfield Argentyńczyk potrzebował trochę czasu na adaptację i uporanie się z problemami zdrowotnymi, ale już ubiegły sezon przyniósł w jego przypadku przełom. Ligowy dorobek trzech goli i sześciu asyst zdążył pobić w trwających rozgrywkach, bo w portugalskiej ekstraklasie cieszył się już z sześciu trafień i czterech ostatnich podań. Benfica może polegać na Prestiannim, którego znaczenie mocno wzrosło jeszcze za kadencji wspomnianego wcześniej Mourinho. Portugalskie media podkreślają, że 20-latek dojrzał, a w jego postawie można dostrzec większą dyscyplinę oraz odpowiednie nastawienie do pracy. Na murawie pozostaje odważny, poszukuje pojedynków z rywalami, ale nie zamyka się tylko na funkcjonowanie na boku. Ochoczo schodzi do środka, gdzie jest w stanie popisać się prostopadłym dograniem. Jego potencjał w ojczyźnie oceniano niezwykle wysoko i nie było przypadkiem, że Orły rywalizowały z powodzeniem o pozyskanie tego piłkarza z, m.in. Chelsea, Ajaxem czy PSV. Teraz zbierają tego owoce, a Prestianni z pewnością nie powiedział jeszcze ostatniego słowa. Clement Lenglet 31-letni stoper bezsprzecznie posiada jedno z najciekawszych CV w całej drużynie Benfiki. Przebywający na wypożyczeniu z Atletico Madryt Francuz najwięcej występów w karierze uzbierał w hiszpańskiej La Lidze, a w tym kraju grając przez cztery lata w FC Barcelonie podnosił każde możliwe krajowe trofeum. W późniejszych sezonach miał okazję sprawdzić się w Premier League w Tottenhamie oraz Aston Villi, by powrócić do Hiszpanii, ale już do jej stolicy. Od lipca jest piłkarzem czwartkowego rywala Niebiesko-Białych, pozostając pierwszym wyborem Marco Silvy na środku obrony. Jego pozycji w drużynie nie zmieniła czerwona kartka obejrzana we wrześniowym ligowym hicie z FC Porto, kiedy to osłabiony przez niego już w pierwszej połowie zespół doznał jedynej porażki w bieżących rozgrywkach Liga Portugal. Do jego poczynań wnosi dużo spokoju pod presją przeciwnika, umiejętność czytania gry i świetnego ustawienia.
